national.line: A California family was reunited with their cocker spaniel Corduroy seven years after the dog disappeared. Corduroy never did go out of style.
A flea-ridden cat rescued by a charity is now a life-saving blood donor for a kitten. That's one hero with whiskers.
An 86-year-old man and his dog were rescued after their sailboat was disabled hundreds of miles off California. Good thing the dog made the crew list.
A police officer bought a surprise birthday cake for a one-year-old girl. Frosting on top of a good deed.
Billy Joel thought "Just the Way You Are" was too mushy and wanted to scrap it, until Linda Ronstadt asked if he was out of his mind. Good call, Linda.
A Tennessee sheriff's office is hunting a mystery monkey seen running across a field near a resident's home. No word yet on whether it's monkeying around.

pride.label: Principal Award
pride.line: Julie Routh, a Bolivar resident and principal at Sherwood Elementary in Springfield, won the MOSHAPE Administrator of the Year Award for backing health and physical education programs. Gold medal for gym class.

pride.label: All-State
pride.line: Bolivar golfer Brielyn Hines placed seventh at state and earned all-state honors, while in tennis Jillian Horner took fourth in singles and Adelyn Seay and Kayla Goodman took fourth in doubles. The Lady Liberators have game.

pride.label: World Champion
pride.line: Victoria Moroski, a 17-year-old from Lake of the Ozarks, won individual gold in the Under-18 Skim division at the world wakesurfing championships in Hangzhou, China, and helped Team USA win team gold too. She really made a splash.

local.line: Chick-fil-A opens its first Osage Beach location Thursday, Nov. 5, and customers dressed in cow-themed attire get a free entree. Time to dust off the cow costume.
Veterans and active-duty military get one free round of golf at Spring Hollow Golf Course on Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov. 11. A thank-you with a tee time.
Camdenton city hall's phone and internet service will be down from 8 a.m. to noon Wednesday during a planned interruption. Good time to write a letter instead.
Ameren is warning people not to push fall leaves into Lake of the Ozarks because piles of them can create real problems for water quality. Rake it, don't lake it.

music.line: Ella Langley and Kacey Musgraves are on the soundtrack to the new Hunger Games movie. May the odds be ever in country's favor.
Riley Green released acoustic performances from his new 19-song album That's Just Me. Stripped-down still sounds good.
Riley Green called contestant Allie Rae a "little mini Reba" after her Lainey Wilson cover on The Voice. Reba just got a tiny sidekick.
Blake Shelton skips the seven-mile drive from the airport to his Oklahoma ranch and sends a helicopter to pick up his guests. Nothing says welcome like rotor blades.
Morgan Wallen now has his own 24/7 SiriusXM channel, called Morgan Wallen Radio, which he curates himself. The request line must be easy.
Shaboozey says Dolly Parton helped shape his country roots through his Nigerian father. Dolly really does get around.
Tyler Hubbard will headline K92.3's Jingle Jam at the Apopka Amphitheater in Florida. Sleigh bells meet steel guitars.
Garth Brooks added a third Hamilton show to his Canadian tour. Canada can't get enough of those friends in low places.
Joe Henley earned a standing ovation from all the coaches on The Voice with a Keith Whitley cover. High praise from a tough room.
Maren Morris finally watched Home Alone after 28 years and wants to start a film club for iconic movies she's never seen. Kevin would approve.
Craig Morgan salutes Toby Keith, American soldiers and the music that made him on his new album My Country. Flags and guitars, a good mix.
Zeus the dog protected Minnesota homeowner Bailey Jacobson from a surprise black bear in her driveway. That's one very good boy.

weird.line: Firefighters in Texas rescued a raccoon spotted high up in a tree with its head stuck in a hollow. That's one nosy raccoon.
A Detroit man spent over 10 years building an 11,578-pound rubber band ball, now certified the world's largest. That's a lot of snap decisions.
A 60-year-old Pennsylvania man set a Guinness World Record by attending 1,207 movie screenings in one year, about 3.3 movies a day. His popcorn budget must be huge.
Seed company Row7 has a potato that tastes like roast chicken. Dinner and a side, all in one.
A homeowner was stunned when a solar installer delivered 23 panels early and left them unattended in the driveway. Free sunshine, no assembly required.
Rescued bear cubs in Colorado are eating 2,000 pounds of fruit a week because drought wiped out wild food. Their grocery bill needs a budget meeting.
Scientists detected dinosaur blood cells in a 115-million-year-old fossil. That's a very old blood draw.
A 10,000-year-old fossilized mastodon was found in a creek. Hope somebody was only out wading.
A Bosnian electrician rescued a two-kilogram bear in 2019, and the 150-kilogram bear still tries to climb on his lap. Lap dog, extra large.

humor.line: Archaeologist Howard Carter found King Tut's tomb in Egypt's Valley of the Kings in 1922. That's one very old game of hide-and-seek.
The Easy-Bake Oven, introduced by Kenner in 1963, originally used an ordinary light bulb as its heat source. Talk about a bright idea.

Dr. Marthenia "Tina" Dupree, known as "The Chicken Lady," spent twelve years as Director of Community Relations and Training at one of the largest chicken restaurants in the world. Now that's a job worth crowing about.
Today is the day you can give in to your sweet tooth and eat as much candy as you want. The leftover Halloween bucket just got a promotion.
Begun in 2017, it kicks off Eat Smart Month and is part of the American Heart Association's Healthy for Good movement. Right after Halloween, that's bold timing.
The first doughnuts in America were little "nuts" of dough brought to New England by Pilgrims who learned to make them in Holland. Even the Pilgrims had priorities.
It started after Bank of America announced a $5 monthly debit card fee in 2011, and people got so mad they urged everyone to move their money to credit unions. Five bucks can start a movement.
Sisters Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti, founders of the website How to be a Redhead, created it to help redheads love their hair. Finally, a holiday that glows.
It's for men who don't usually cook to try making dinner. Ladies, keep the smoke alarm handy.
American football grew out of rugby football and soccer, and its rules changed a lot over time. Even football started as a rough draft.
James Naismith, born in Almonte, Ontario in 1861, invented basketball by nailing peach baskets to the balcony at each end of a YMCA gym. Peach baskets: the original hoop dream.
Nachos trace back to 1943, when the wives of ten soldiers from Fort Duncan, Texas ate at Club Victoria across the border and met chef Ignacio "Nacho." Lucky his nickname wasn't Broccoli.
Adolphe Sax, a Belgian instrument maker who moved to Paris in 1842 to start a business, made a saxophone first meant for military bands. Marching just got a lot smoother.
Florida attorney Nader Anise created it in 2001, and lawyer jokes are not allowed. Objection sustained.
The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt after a cartoon showed him refusing to shoot a bear on a 1902 hunting trip. Best press that bear ever got.
In 1973, a New Jersey hearing officer ruled that keeping girls out of Little League was illegal, a year after 11-year-old Marcia Pepe played three games. Strike three for the old rule.
Before paper, people wrote on clay tablets and then on papyrus made from reed stems. Imagine dropping one in the bathtub.
Puns have been around for thousands of years, showing up in Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian and Mayan hieroglyphics. The groans are just as old.
Cappuccino is named for the Capuchin friars, whose reddish-brown hoods matched the color of the drink. Their wardrobe made the menu.
The pupusa, El Salvador's national dish, is connected to cooking tools found at a site buried by volcanic ash about 2,000 years ago. Talk about a recipe that lasts.
Dr. Seuss's Fox in Socks is the classic way to celebrate because it's packed with tongue twisters. Say it three times fast. We'll wait.
Carl Sagan, born in 1934, hosted the 1980 PBS series Cosmos, the most widely viewed PBS program of its time. He made space look easy.
Scrapple was created by the Pennsylvania Dutch, who emigrated from Germany and Switzerland in the 17th and 18th centuries. Waste not, want not, apparently.
AT&T devised area codes in the 1940s, and the North American Numbering Plan made them official in 1947. Long before anybody had a cell phone.
Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli, born in 1445, wrote the first printed book to include double-entry bookkeeping. Every debit finally got a credit.
New York City renamed a corner of Lincoln Square "123 Sesame Street" in 2009 for the show's fortieth anniversary. Can you tell me how to get there?
The word "cupcake" was first used in 1828, and a dessert like it showed up in American Cookery in 1796. Good things take a while.
